jungle.definition: n. a location marked by an intense competition and struggle for survival\nn. an impenetrable equatorial forest
jungle.translation: n. 丛林, 杂乱的一堆, 弱肉强食的地方

examples.en: When we looked down, we saw a concrete jungle.
examples.zh: 我们往下看，是一片水泥丛林。

examples.en: The lion is the king of the jungle.
examples.zh: 狮子是丛林之王。

examples.en: He wrote a book about a jungle adventure.
examples.zh: 他写了一本关于丛林冒险的书。

phrase.cn: 水泥丛林；立体丛林；混凝土建成的野兽世界

junior.definition:
n. term of address for a disrespectful and annoying male
n. a third-year undergraduate
n. the younger of two persons
n. a son who has the same first name as his father
junior.translation: n. 年少者, 地位较低者, 大学三年级学生\na. 年少的, 下级的, 后进的

examples.en: He eventually married an Italian woman ten years his junior.
examples.zh: 他最终和一个比他小十岁的意大利女人结了婚。

examples.en: Junior, why don't we go into a group together?
examples.zh: Junior，我们为何不一起加入同一个小组呢

examples.en: He's just a normal junior high school student, not particularly intelligent.
examples.zh: 他只不过是个普普通通的中学生，不算特别聪明。

phrase.cn: n. 两年制专科学校，大专

jurisdiction.definition: n. in law; the territory within which power can be exercised
jurisdiction.translation: n. 司法权, 审判权, 管辖权\n[经] 法律管辖权, 审判权

examples.en: The judge said that the case was outside of his jurisdiction.
Jurisdictions must justify their decisions as defined by law.
Different jurisdictions often have distinct definitions of justifiable homicide.

jury.definition: n. a body of citizens sworn to give a true verdict according to the evidence presented in a court of law\nn. a committee appointed to judge a competition
jury.translation: n. 陪审团, 评判委员会\na. 应急的

examples.en: The jury looked shocked.
examples.zh: 陪审团看起来很震惊。

phrase.cn: 在陪审团作陪审员时间；陪审员的义务

just.definition:
a. used especially of what is legally or ethically right or proper or fitting
r. only a moment ago
r. absolutely
r. exactly at this moment or the moment described;
just.translation: a. 正直的, 合理的, 正确的, 应得的\nadv. 刚刚, 正好, 仅仅

examples.en: I may give up soon and just take a nap.
examples.zh: 也许我会马上放弃然后去打盹。

examples.en: He was just on the verge of going to sleep.
examples.zh: 他快要睡了。

examples.en: All of them are just here to pick up girls.
examples.zh: 他们都是为了泡妞才来的。

justice.definition: n. the quality of being just or fair\nn. judgment involved in the determination of rights and the assignment of rewards and punishments
justice.translation: n. 正义, 公平, 公正, 正确, 司法, 审判

examples.en: Unity, justice and freedom are the pledge of fortune.
examples.zh: 团结、公正和自由是幸福的保证。

examples.en: It is justice, not charity, that is wanting in the world.
examples.zh: 世界需要的是公正，不是施舍。

examples.en: He believed that the war was fought in the cause of justice.
examples.zh: 他相信，战争是为了正义而战。

syno.tran: 司法，法律制裁；正义；法官，[法]审判员

justification.definition: n. something (such as a fact or circumstance) that shows an action to be reasonable or necessary\nn. a statement in explanation of some action or belief\nn. the act of defending or explaining or making excuses for by reasoning
justification.translation: n. 辩护, 证明正当, 释罪\n[计] 调整

examples.en: This is hardly a justification for betraying your friend's confidence.
There can be no justification for harming a child.
You have no justification to say something like that.

justify.definition: v. show to be reasonable or provide adequate ground for\nv. show to be right by providing justification or proof\nv. adjust the spaces between words
justify.translation: vt. 替...辩护, 证明\nvi. 证明合法\n[计] 段落重排, 两端对齐

examples.en: The end does not always justify the means.
examples.zh: 为了正当目的并非总是可以不择手段.

examples.en: The end justifies the means.
examples.zh: 为了正当目的可以不择手段。

juvenile.definition: n. a young person, not fully developed\na. of or relating to or characteristic of or appropriate for children or young people
juvenile.translation: n. 少年, 少年读物\na. 少年的, 不成熟的, 适于少年的

examples.en: Juvenile crimes have been increasing recently.
examples.zh: 少年犯罪最近一直在增长。

phrase.cn: 青少年糖尿病；幼年型糖尿病

jargon.definition: n. specialized technical terminology characteristic of a particular subject
jargon.translation: n. 专门术语, 行话, 梦话, 土语\n[计] 行话

examples.en: By using this corporate jargon, Mark wanted to sound smarter.
Chinook Jargon was once widespread in the Pacific Northwest.
The talk was peppered with scientific jargon that no one understood.

jest.definition: n. activity characterized by good humor
jest.translation: n. 笑柄, 笑话\nvi. 讲笑话, 嘲笑, 开玩笑\nvt. 嘲笑

examples.en: Many a true word is spoken in jest.
examples.zh: 笑谈之中有至理。

jolt.definition: n. a sudden jarring impact\nv. move or cause to move with a sudden jerky motion\nv. disturb (someone's) composure
jolt.translation: n. 震摇, 摇动, 颠簸\nvi. 颠簸而行, 震摇\nvt. 使颠簸, 使慌张, 猛击

examples.en: He hit me with a hard right which jolted me.
A loud noise jolted me awake from a deep sleep.
Suddenly I felt something like a jolt.

jubilant.definition: s joyful and proud especially because of triumph or success\ns full of high-spirited delight
jubilant.translation: a. 欢呼的, 喜洋洋的

examples.en: A festive, jubilant crowd thronged Berlin’s historic Brandenburg Gate.
The crowd is jubilant.
I got a thesaurus as a present and I feel very happy, glad, cheerful, jovial, jubilant and merry.

judicial.definition: s. decreed by or proceeding from a court of justice\na. belonging or appropriate to the office of a judge\na. relating to the administration of justice or the function of a judge
judicial.translation: a. 法庭的, 公正的, 审判上的, 司法的\n[法] 司法的, 审判上的, 法官的

examples.en: Maltese is used in legal and judicial proceedings in Malta.
Some people say that the judicial system is rigged.
It's not a judicial reform; it's a judicial takeover.

juncture.definition: n. an event that occurs at a critical time\nn. a crisis situation or point in time when a critical decision must be made
juncture.translation: n. 接合, 连接, 接缝

examples.en: He came to an important juncture in his life.
He arrived at an important juncture in his life.
I don't want to jump into any conclusions at this juncture.

jellyfish.definition: n. any of numerous usually marine and free-swimming coelenterates that constitute the sexually reproductive forms of hydrozoans and scyphozoans
jellyfish.translation: n. 水母, 海蜇, 意志薄弱的人\n[医] 海蛰, 水母

examples.en: The fisherman caught a purple jellyfish in his net.
examples.zh: 渔民用他的网捕到了一只紫色的水母。

jeopardise.definition: v pose a threat to; present a danger to
jeopardise.translation: vt. 使受危险, 危及, 危害\n[法] 使受危害, 使陷入危险, 危及

jeopardy.definition: n a source of danger; a possibility of incurring loss or misfortune
jeopardy.translation: n. 危难, 危险\n[法] 危险, 危难, 危险处境

examples.en: Tom Jackson will be the new host of Jeopardy!
Yanni was in jeopardy somehow by living with Skura.
I'm afraid going into their yard will put me in jeopardy.

jetlag.translation: n. 时差综合症（跨时区高速飞行后生理节奏的破坏）

examples.en: I am feeling jetlagged.
I'm still feeling jetlagged.

jockey.definition:
n. someone employed to ride horses in horse races
n. an operator of some vehicle or machine or apparatus
v. compete (for an advantage or a position)
v. ride a racehorse as a professional jockey
jockey.translation: n. 赛马骑师, 驾驶员, 操作工\nvt. 骗, 瞒, 驾驶, 移动\nvi. 当赛马的骑师

examples.en: I know that Tom used to be a disc jockey.
I know Tom used to be a disc jockey.
He is out and away the best jockey.

joyous.definition: a. full of or characterized by joy
joyous.translation: a. 快乐的, 高兴的

examples.en: To Boris's joyous surprise, there was a payphone there.
They reached the castle in safety, amid a thousand joyous acclamations.
Spring in Algeria is a joyous time.

juror.definition: n. someone who serves (or waits to be called to serve) on a jury
juror.translation: n. 陪审员, 审查委员\n[法] 陪审员, 陪审官, 宣誓者

examples.en: Sami's lawyer told the jurors that cops arrested the wrong person.
Sami had many jurors lobbying on his behalf.
The twelfth juror is missing.

judiciary.definition: n. persons who administer justice\nn. the system of law courts that administer justice and constitute the judicial branch of government
judiciary.translation: a. 司法的, 法院的, 法官的\nn. 司法部, 司法系统, 法官

examples.en: Netanyahu wants to severely curtail the powers of the judiciary.
The judiciary should not become merely an extension of the legislative branch.
An independent judiciary is one of the key pillars of a functional democracy.

jack.definition:
n. a small worthless amount
n. a small ball at which players aim in lawn bowling
n. an electrical device consisting of a connector socket designed for the insertion of a plug
n. game equipment consisting of one of several small six-pointed metal pieces that are picked up while bouncing a ball in the game of jacks
jack.translation:
n. 插座, 千斤顶, 男人
vt. 抬起, 提醒, 扛举, 增加, 提高, 放弃
a. 雄的
[计] 插座

examples.en: She said that she would visit Jack with her sisters.
examples.zh: 她说她会和她的姐妹们一起去看望杰克。

examples.en: The red house is the one that Jack built.
examples.zh: 那个红房子就是杰克盖的房子。

examples.en: Bring the jack over. I'll jack up the car.
examples.zh: 把千斤顶拿过来，我要把汽车撑起来。

jazz.definition: n. a genre of popular music that originated in New Orleans around 1900 and developed through increasingly complex styles\nn. a style of dance music popular in the 1920s; similar to New Orleans jazz but played by large bands\nv. play something in the style of jazz
jazz.translation:
n. 爵士乐, 喧闹
a. 爵士乐的, 喧吵的
vi. 演奏爵士乐, 跳爵士舞, 游荡
vt. 奏爵士乐, 使活泼

examples.en: Jazz fusion is a combination of rock and jazz.
examples.zh: 融合爵士是摇滚乐与爵士乐的融合。

examples.en: Tom started playing jazz after studying classical music for many years.
examples.zh: 在学习古典音乐多年后，汤姆开始演奏爵士了。

examples.en: I like to listen to music, especially jazz.
examples.zh: 我喜欢听音乐，特别是爵士音乐。

jean.definition: n. (usually plural) close-fitting trousers of heavy denim for manual work or casual wear
jean.translation: n. 牛仔裤, 牛仔布, 斜纹棉布

examples.en: Jean has fallen out with Paul over the education of their children.
examples.zh: Jean和Paul为他们孩子的教育吵了起来。

examples.en: Jean and Kate are twins.
examples.zh: Jean和Kate是双胞胎。

jelly.definition: n. a preserve made of the jelled juice of fruit\nn. any substance having the consistency of jelly or gelatin
jelly.translation: n. 果冻, 果冻甜食, 胶状物\nv. (使)结冻, (使)成胶状

examples.en: What he likes is jelly.
examples.zh: 他喜欢的是果冻。

examples.en: I like grape jelly best.
examples.zh: 我最喜欢吃葡萄果冻。

jewellery.definition: n an adornment (as a bracelet or ring or necklace) made of precious metals and set with gems (or imitation gems)
jewellery.translation: n. 宝石, 贵重饰物, 珠宝, 宝石饰物, 受珍视的人/物, 宝贝, 有价值的人/物

examples.en: Sir and Miss, what type of jewellery are you looking to buy?
examples.zh: 先生小姐，你们买点什么首饰？

examples.en: She wears a lot of jewellery.
examples.zh: 她戴很多珠宝。

examples.en: She's wearing a lot of jewellery.
examples.zh: 她戴著很多珠宝。

jingle.definition: n. a metallic sound\nv. make a sound typical of metallic objects
jingle.translation: n. 叮当声\nv. (使)作叮当声, (使)押韵

examples.en: Give me a jingle when you have a chance.
I shake the money box to hear it jingle.
Yanni was jingling a key ring with keys on it.

judgement.definition:
n the legal document stating the reasons for a judicial decision
n an opinion formed by judging something
n the cognitive process of reaching a decision or drawing conclusions
n the mental ability to understand and discriminate between relations
n the capacity to assess situations or circumstances shrewdly and to draw sound conclusions
n (law) the determination by a court of competent jurisdiction on matters submitted to it
n the act of judging or assessing a person or situation or event
judgement.translation: n. 审判, 判决, 判断\n[经] 判定, 审定, 鉴定

examples.en: We can rely on his judgement.
examples.zh: 我们可以信赖他的判断。

examples.en: You are correct in your judgement.
examples.zh: 你的判断是正确的。

examples.en: The judgement went against the government.
examples.zh: 判决对政府不利。

jug.definition: n. a large bottle with a narrow mouth\nn. the quantity contained in a jug\nv. stew in an earthenware jug
jug.translation: n. 水壶, 监牢, 模仿夜莺的叫声\nvt. 放入壶中, 炖, 关押\nvi. 模仿夜莺叫

examples.en: Once your jug is cracked, better put flowers in it.
She left for the fountain to fill her jug.
Benedito carried a jug of water to the picnic.

junk.definition: n. any of various Chinese boats with a high poop and lugsails
junk.translation: n. 垃圾, 乌七八糟的东西, 舢板\n[计] 清除

examples.en: Tom used to eat a lot of junk food.
examples.zh: 汤姆以前经常吃很多垃圾食品。

examples.en: Instead of eating real food, we just ate junk food all day.
examples.zh: 我们整天吃的都是杂七杂八的零嘴，并没有甚么正规的食物下过肚。

examples.en: Tom has accumulated a lot of junk.
examples.zh: 汤姆屯了很多垃圾。
